title: Introduce rw-private-dr CLI with backup create/verify + restore plan scaffolding
author: Connor O'Brien
description: ## Summary This PR introduces an initial `rw-private-dr` command surface in the private installer repo to support Day-2 backup/restore workflows for Redwood Private. Specifically: adds CLI subcommands for `backup create`, `backup verify`, and `restore plan`; adds argument parsing + validation; defines an initial DR config schema (YAML) and mapping into the existing installer config; and updates the repo README with early operator-facing usage examples. This PR intentionally does **not** attempt to fully implement backup/restore logic end-to-end (DB dumps, object storage adapters, retention, PITR, etc.). Those will land in follow-on PRs, but we need a stable CLI contract + config format to unblock docs/runbooks and early integration testing. ## Motivation / context We’re standardizing backup/restore for Private deployments across VPC and on-prem (incl. restricted and partially air-gapped environments). Operators need a single, versioned CLI that: (1) validates config and preconditions before taking actions, (2) produces deterministic artifacts/metadata for restore planning and verification, and (3) supports dry-run planning with clear output for runbooks and incident response. Linear: ENG-4821 (epic), ENG-4841 (`backup create`), ENG-4848 (`restore plan/execute`). ## CLI overview New top-level command: `rw-private-dr` (installed/built alongside existing installer binaries). Commands included in this PR: - `rw-private-dr backup create` - Creates a backup bundle and a `backup-manifest.json` describing what was captured. In this PR, the implementation is a scaffold: it writes the manifest, collects cluster identity + timestamps, and (if `--output` points to a local path) writes a placeholder bundle directory layout. Actual DB dumps and artifact snapshots will be added in follow-ups. - `rw-private-dr backup verify` - Verifies a backup bundle/manifest: schema validation, required files present, checksum file existence (future), and basic sanity checks (created_at, cluster_id match when provided). - `rw-private-dr restore plan` - Produces a plan (ordered steps) for a restore run, including required inputs and prechecks. This is a dry-run only: it does not modify the cluster. Output can be `text` (default) or `json` for automation. Example usage: `rw-private-dr backup create --config /etc/redwood/private.yaml --output /var/lib/redwood/backups/$(date +%F)` `rw-private-dr backup verify --input /var/lib/redwood/backups/2025-10-10` `rw-private-dr restore plan --config /etc/redwood/private.yaml --input /var/lib/redwood/backups/2025-10-10 --format json` ## Config schema Adds a `dr:` block to the installer config (YAML). Initial fields are focused on enabling validation + future wiring; we avoid embedding secrets directly and support env var references. Proposed schema (excerpt): ```yaml dr: enabled: true backup: output: type: local # local|s3|minio|nfs (non-local adapters follow in later PRs) path: /var/lib/redwood/backups encryption: enabled: true provider: local # local|kms (kms later) restore: allow_in_place: true # gates future restore execute behavior in runbooks ``` Notes: - Validation enforces that `dr.enabled=true` must include `dr.backup.output` fields. - For now, `type=local` is the only fully supported output target in code; other types are accepted for schema compatibility but will return a clear "not implemented" error at runtime. - Any field that could contain credentials is explicitly modeled to support env var expansion later; this PR avoids printing raw config on error paths and redacts common keys. ## Docs Updates `README.md` with an "(Experimental) Private DR" section that: - Defines what the CLI does/doesn’t do in this phase - Shows examples for `backup create/verify` and `restore plan` - Calls out expected follow-ons: storage adapters, Postgres dump/PITR, retention, Helm CronJobs/Jobs integration, and maintenance-mode gates. ## Implementation details - Uses cobra for command structure and `pflag` for flags. - Adds `pkg/dr/` with: - `config.go`: schema structs + validation - `manifest.go`: manifest definition + writer/reader - `plan.go`: restore plan model + renderers (text/json) - Adds common error formatting with actionable operator messages (missing directories, permission denied, invalid YAML, etc.). - Adds `--log-format` and `--log-level` consistent with existing installer conventions. - Adds `--format json` for `restore plan` output to support future CI/game-day automation. ## Safety / security - No secrets are written into the manifest. Manifest includes cluster identifier, created timestamp, CLI version, and list of components captured (placeholders for now). - CLI avoids echoing entire config on validation failures. - Adds a `redactForLogs()` helper and basic tests ensuring common credential keys don’t appear in error strings. ## Testing - Unit tests for: config validation, manifest read/write, plan rendering output stability. - Basic CLI smoke tests in CI: `--help` output, invalid config path, and a create+verify loop against a temp directory. ## Follow-ups (not in this PR) - Add storage adapters (S3/minio/NFS) + server-side encryption options - Implement Postgres dump + PITR scaffolding + WAL archiving wiring - Implement real bundle layout with checksums and partial-upload prevention - Add `restore execute` (blocked on maintenance mode + validation gates) - Integrate with Helm (CronJob/Job) and Terraform examples - Cross-link Confluence runbooks and add runbook URLs to `restore plan` output for operators ## Screenshots / output (sample) `rw-private-dr restore plan --input ./backup-2025-10-10` prints: 1. Validate backup manifest + checksums 2. Confirm maintenance mode enabled (manual step in this phase) 3. Restore control-plane DB (placeholder) 4. Restore object artifacts (placeholder) 5. Restart control plane services (placeholder) 6. Run health checks and smoke tests (placeholder) ## Checklist - [x] Unit tests added - [x] CLI help output reviewed for operator clarity - [x] Error paths avoid leaking secrets - [x] README updated with experimental disclaimer

review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): The `restore plan` output is the right direction. Can we make sure it prints the *exact* next command(s) operators should run, not just conceptual steps? Connor O'Brien (author): Agreed. In this PR I kept it conceptual to avoid committing to flags we may change, but I can add "recommended command" lines for the steps we control (e.g., `backup verify` + future `restore execute`). I added a small tweak to include the computed input path and suggested verify command. Michael Nguyen (review): Config schema: do we want `dr.enabled` or should this be implied by the presence of `dr:`? I’m worried about folks setting `enabled: false` and thinking backups still run via Helm CronJob later. Connor O'Brien (author): Good point. I left `enabled` so we can gate validation and avoid surprising users when the feature isn’t configured. For Helm integration we’ll likely require `enabled=true` for rendering resources. I added a README callout that CronJobs (future) will be gated by `dr.enabled`. Marcus Lin (review): Please double-check no secrets can leak in error messages. I see `fmt.Errorf("invalid config: %v", err)` patterns that might include raw YAML excerpts. Connor O'Brien (author): Updated error wrapping to avoid including raw YAML decode errors that echo input. Also added a redaction helper + tests asserting credential-like keys don’t appear in returned errors. Vivek Kulkarni (review): Can we add an explicit disclaimer: this does not yet back up Postgres or model artifacts, it only scaffolds the CLI + manifest. We should avoid customers/operators assuming this is a full DR solution. Connor O'Brien (author): Added "Experimental" section in README and bolded limitations in PR summary. Elliot Price (review): README looks good. Please keep the terminology aligned with the planned Confluence pages (backup bundle / manifest / restore plan). Also can you add a short "Terminology" subsection? Connor O'Brien (author): Added a short terminology block and updated wording to "bundle" consistently. Approvals: Rafael Mendes approved; Michael Nguyen approved after edits; Marcus Lin approved after redaction changes; Vivek Kulkarni approved with note to link Confluence once pages are published; Elliot Price approved.
